title: European Union Artificial Intelligence Act enters into force
statusNote: Obligations apply in stages; most provisions apply from 2 August 2026 and some from 2027.

scores.rationale: Immediate effects were limited because obligations are phased in. Long-term significance is high: it is the first comprehensive horizontal legal framework for AI, binding across 27 member states and applicable to foreign providers serving the EU market.

account.outcome: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the Artificial Intelligence Act, was published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 12 July 2024 and entered into force on 1 August 2024 in all 27 member states. It classifies AI systems by risk, prohibits certain practices, and sets obligations for high-risk systems and for providers of general-purpose AI models, with application staggered between 2025 and 2027.
account.significance: The Act is the first comprehensive, horizontal legal framework for artificial intelligence adopted by a major jurisdiction. Because it applies to any provider placing systems on the EU market, its requirements reach well beyond Europe.
account.longTerm: The regulation establishes a reference model for governing AI by risk category. Its practical effect will depend on implementing standards, national enforcement and later amendments, but it fixes a legal baseline against which future AI governance elsewhere is likely to be compared.

title: Egypt certified malaria-free by the World Health Organization
goodNewsRationale: Certification requires proof that indigenous transmission has been interrupted nationwide for at least three consecutive years: a measured public health outcome for a population of more than 100 million.

scores.rationale: Little changed on the day of certification, since transmission had already stopped. Long-term significance is substantial: elimination in a country of over 100 million after nearly a century of effort, and the first certification in the Eastern Mediterranean Region since 2010.

account.outcome: On 20 October 2024 the World Health Organization certified Egypt as malaria-free. Certification is granted when a country demonstrates that indigenous transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes has been interrupted nationwide for at least three consecutive years. Egypt became the third country in WHO's Eastern Mediterranean Region to be certified, after the United Arab Emirates and Morocco.
account.significance: Malaria had been present in Egypt since antiquity. Elimination followed nearly a century of surveillance, vector control and free diagnosis and treatment, sustained through ecological changes such as those introduced by the Aswan High Dam.
account.longTerm: The certification shows that elimination is achievable in a populous country with a long history of transmission. Maintaining the status depends on continued surveillance and rapid response to imported cases.

title: COP29 adopts a new collective goal for climate finance

scores.rationale: The decision sets the framework for climate finance to developing countries until 2035. Its long-term weight is tempered by the gap between the agreed figure and the needs stated by developing countries, and by uncertainty over delivery.

account.outcome: At the UN Climate Change Conference in Baku, Azerbaijan, parties adopted the New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance in the early hours of 24 November 2024. Developed countries are to take the lead in mobilising at least USD 300 billion a year for developing countries by 2035, replacing the earlier USD 100 billion goal. The decision also calls for efforts by all actors to scale finance to USD 1.3 trillion a year by 2035.
account.significance: The goal defines the main finance commitment under the Paris Agreement for the coming decade. Several developing-country delegations stated at adoption that the amount was insufficient.
account.longTerm: The figure will shape the ambition of national climate plans and the credibility of multilateral climate cooperation. Whether it is met, and how much takes the form of public grants rather than loans or private flows, remains to be seen.

title: Government of Bashar al-Assad falls in Syria
statusNote: This entry records the end of the Assad government. The subsequent political transition is a separate, unresolved process.

scores.rationale: The collapse ended more than five decades of rule by the Assad family and altered the position of regional and external powers. It directly affects the population of Syria and the millions of Syrian refugees abroad.

account.outcome: On 8 December 2024 opposition forces entered Damascus following an offensive that began in late November and captured Aleppo, Hama and Homs. President Bashar al-Assad left the country; Russian state media reported that he and his family were granted asylum in Russia. The government's collapse ended more than five decades of rule by the Assad family.
account.significance: The event closed a defining chapter of the Syrian civil war, which began in 2011, and removed a government that had been a central ally of Iran and Russia in the region.
account.longTerm: The fall of the government changed the regional balance of power and opened the question of Syria's future political order, reconstruction and the return of refugees. Those outcomes are not yet settled and are outside the scope of this entry.

title: Quantum error correction demonstrated below the surface-code threshold
goodNewsRationale: A peer-reviewed experimental result that resolves a long-standing open question in quantum computing, advancing scientific knowledge.

scores.rationale: No practical application follows directly. Long-term significance rests on the result being a necessary condition for fault-tolerant quantum computers; the scale required for useful computation has not been reached, and the result comes from a single research group.

account.outcome: On 9 December 2024 Nature published results from Google Quantum AI and collaborators showing surface-code quantum memories operating below the error-correction threshold on the Willow superconducting processor. As the code distance increased from 3 to 5 to 7, the logical error rate was roughly halved at each step, and the largest logical qubit outlived the best physical qubit.
account.significance: Since quantum error correction was proposed in the 1990s, it has been expected that adding qubits would reduce errors only once hardware operated below a critical threshold. This experiment provided a clear demonstration of that behaviour in a surface code.
account.longTerm: Below-threshold operation is a prerequisite for building large, fault-tolerant quantum computers. The result does not establish when such machines will exist, but it removes a fundamental obstacle on the path toward them.

title: South Korea's Constitutional Court removes President Yoon Suk Yeol from office

scores.rationale: The ruling resolved a constitutional crisis in a democracy of about 51 million people and triggered an early presidential election. Its long-term significance lies in the judicial affirmation of limits on emergency powers.

account.outcome: On 4 April 2025 South Korea's Constitutional Court unanimously upheld the National Assembly's impeachment of President Yoon Suk Yeol and removed him from office. The court found that his declaration of martial law on 3 December 2024, and the deployment of troops to the National Assembly, violated the constitution. The ruling required a presidential election within 60 days.
account.significance: Yoon became the second South Korean president to be removed through impeachment. The case was resolved through constitutional procedures, with the legislature lifting martial law within hours and the court ruling on the impeachment.
account.longTerm: The decision sets a clear judicial precedent on the limits of presidential emergency powers in South Korea and is likely to be cited in future debates on martial law and the separation of powers.

title: World Health Assembly adopts the WHO Pandemic Agreement
statusNote: Adopted, but not yet open for signature: in May 2026 the Assembly extended negotiations on the required Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing annex.

scores.rationale: Adoption created no immediate obligations, since the agreement cannot enter into force until an annex is adopted and 60 states ratify. Long-term significance is high if it enters into force, as a binding global framework for pandemic preparedness.

account.outcome: On 20 May 2025 the 78th World Health Assembly adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement by consensus, after more than three years of negotiation prompted by COVID-19. The text had been approved in committee the previous day by 124 votes in favour, none against and 11 abstentions. It is the second agreement negotiated under Article 19 of the WHO Constitution, after the 2003 Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.
account.significance: The agreement sets principles for prevention, preparedness and more equitable access to vaccines, treatments and diagnostics during future pandemics. It was adopted without the participation of the United States.
account.longTerm: Its effect depends on adoption of the pathogen-sharing annex, which was not concluded by May 2026, and on ratification by at least 60 states. If those steps are completed, it would become the principal legal instrument for collective pandemic response.

title: United States approves a twice-yearly injection for HIV prevention
goodNewsRationale: Approval followed two Phase 3 trials in which more than 99.9% of participants receiving the drug remained HIV-negative, a demonstrated health benefit.

scores.rationale: The approval applies in one country, but it establishes the first twice-yearly prevention option and supports further regulatory filings elsewhere. Long-term significance depends on price and on access in high-incidence regions.

account.outcome: On 18 June 2025 the US Food and Drug Administration approved lenacapavir, marketed by Gilead Sciences as Yeztugo, as pre-exposure prophylaxis to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg. It is injected twice a year. Approval rested on the Phase 3 PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2 trials, in which more than 99.9% of participants receiving lenacapavir did not acquire HIV.
account.significance: Existing preventive options require daily pills or injections every two months. A dosing interval of six months addresses adherence, one of the main reasons prevention fails in practice.
account.longTerm: If made widely available, a long-acting option of this efficacy could change the course of HIV prevention globally. That outcome depends on approvals in other countries, manufacturing capacity and pricing in regions with the highest incidence.

title: Suriname certified malaria-free, the first country in the Amazon region
goodNewsRationale: Certification confirms that indigenous transmission has been interrupted for at least three consecutive years; the last locally acquired case was recorded in 2021.

scores.rationale: The population directly affected is small (about 600,000). The long-term significance is regional: it is the first elimination in the Amazon basin, where forest ecology and mobile mining populations make transmission difficult to control.

account.outcome: On 30 June 2025 the World Health Organization certified Suriname as malaria-free, the first country in the Amazon region to receive the certification. The last locally acquired case had been recorded in 2021. Suriname became the twelfth country in the Americas to be certified.
account.significance: Control efforts began in the 1950s. In later decades transmission was concentrated among mobile gold-mining communities in the interior, which the national programme reached through community-based testing and treatment.
account.longTerm: The result demonstrates that elimination is feasible in Amazonian conditions and provides a working model for neighbouring countries. Sustaining it depends on surveillance of imported cases, particularly across borders with countries where malaria remains endemic.

title: International Court of Justice issues advisory opinion on states' climate obligations

scores.rationale: Advisory opinions are not binding and produced no immediate change in emissions. Long-term significance is high: a unanimous, authoritative statement of international law that courts and negotiators are likely to rely on for decades.

account.outcome: On 23 July 2025 the International Court of Justice delivered, unanimously, its advisory opinion on the Obligations of States in respect of Climate Change, requested by the UN General Assembly in 2023. The Court found that states have binding obligations to protect the climate system arising from climate treaties and from customary international law, including a duty to prevent significant environmental harm, and that breaches may constitute internationally wrongful acts.
account.significance: The request originated with Pacific island states. The Court rejected the position that climate treaties are the only applicable law, and treated the 1.5°C limit as the primary agreed temperature goal.
account.longTerm: Although not legally binding, the opinion is the highest judicial interpretation of international climate law. It is expected to inform domestic litigation, future negotiations and claims concerning responsibility for climate damage.

title: Australia's minimum age of 16 for social media accounts takes effect

scores.rationale: The law immediately affected the accounts of a large share of Australian children and the operations of major platforms. Its long-term significance depends on enforcement, on measured effects, and on whether other countries adopt similar rules.

account.outcome: On 10 December 2025 the Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024 took effect in Australia. Designated platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, X and YouTube, must take reasonable steps to prevent people under 16 from creating or keeping accounts, with fines of up to AUD 49.5 million. Penalties apply to platforms, not to children or parents.
account.significance: Australia became the first country to impose a nationwide minimum age for social media accounts. The measure required platforms to deactivate existing accounts and to deploy age-assurance methods at scale.
account.longTerm: The law is a test case for regulating children's access to online platforms by age. Its effects on young people's wellbeing, and the accuracy and privacy implications of age assurance, are not yet established and are actively debated.

title: Bulgaria adopts the euro as the 21st member of the euro area

scores.rationale: The lev had been pegged first to the Deutsche Mark and then to the euro since 1997, which limited the immediate economic shock. Long-term significance is institutional: Bulgaria's central bank joined the Eurosystem and monetary policy for 6.4 million people moved to the European Central Bank.

account.outcome: On 1 January 2026 Bulgaria replaced the lev with the euro and became the 21st member of the euro area. The Council of the European Union had adopted the required legal acts on 8 July 2025, fixing the conversion rate at 1.95583 lev to the euro. The two currencies circulated together during January, and the Bulgarian National Bank joined the Eurosystem.
account.significance: It was the first enlargement of the euro area since Croatia joined in 2023. The changeover took place while an outgoing government was in office and no 2026 budget had been adopted.
account.longTerm: Membership removes exchange-rate risk and transfers monetary policy to the European Central Bank. Public opinion on adoption was divided, with concern about price increases; its economic effects will be measurable only over several years.

title: High Seas Treaty enters into force
statusNote: The treaty's institutions are still being established; the first Conference of the Parties must meet by January 2027.

scores.rationale: Entry into force created a legal basis but no protected areas on the day itself. Long-term significance is high because the treaty is the first binding framework for conserving biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, close to half of the planet's surface.

account.outcome: The Agreement on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction, adopted under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea in 2023, entered into force on 17 January 2026. The 60th ratification had been deposited on 19 September 2025, starting a 120-day period. By mid-January more than 80 states had ratified.
account.significance: Before the treaty, no comprehensive legal framework existed for establishing marine protected areas on the high seas or for requiring environmental impact assessments there.
account.longTerm: The treaty provides the legal means to create high-seas protected areas, share benefits from marine genetic resources and assess the impact of activities in international waters. Its practical effect depends on the institutions now being set up and on participation by major maritime states.

title: WHO prequalifies the first malaria treatment formulated for newborns and young infants
goodNewsRationale: Prequalification certifies quality, safety and efficacy and allows public-sector procurement of a treatment for a group that previously had no dedicated formulation.

scores.rationale: Benefits accrue as procurement and distribution follow. Long-term significance reflects the size of the group concerned: about 30 million babies are born each year in malaria-endemic areas of Africa.

account.outcome: On 24 April 2026 the World Health Organization announced the prequalification of an artemether-lumefantrine formulation for newborns and young infants weighing 2 to 5 kg, the first antimalarial designed specifically for this group. On 14 April WHO had also prequalified three rapid diagnostic tests that detect a different parasite protein, addressing false negatives caused by parasites that no longer produce the protein detected by common tests.
account.significance: Infants had been treated with formulations intended for older children, which increases the risk of dosing errors and toxicity. WHO prequalification enables procurement by UN agencies and other public-sector buyers.
account.longTerm: The formulation closes a long-standing gap in malaria treatment for the youngest patients, among whom the disease is most dangerous. Its effect on mortality will depend on supply and uptake in endemic countries.

title: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva re-elected President of Brazil in runoff
statusNote: The defeated candidate said he would seek annulment of the election. The new term begins on 1 January 2027.

scores.rationale: The result determines the government of Latin America's largest country, with over 200 million people, until 2031. Its long-term significance lies in the continuity of policy and in Brazil's international positioning, which depend on the coming term.

account.outcome: On 25 October 2026 Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers' Party won Brazil's presidential runoff against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party. The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) declared Lula the winner with about 52% of valid votes to Bolsonaro's 48%. Lula had finished second in the first round on 4 October. Bolsonaro rejected the result and announced legal action to annul the election.
account.significance: Lula became the first candidate since the restoration of direct presidential elections in 1989 to win a runoff after trailing in the first round. It is his fourth, non-consecutive term.
account.longTerm: The outcome keeps Brazil's government on its current domestic and foreign-policy course for another four years. The challenge to the result tests the authority of the electoral court in a polarised political climate.

title: Eritrea validated by WHO as having eliminated trachoma as a public health problem
goodNewsRationale: WHO validation follows independent review of survey evidence that elimination thresholds were met across all formerly endemic areas: a measured reduction of a leading infectious cause of blindness.

scores.rationale: The effect is national and builds on results already achieved before validation. Long-term significance comes from removing a cause of irreversible blindness in a country with limited health infrastructure, and from the low-cost model it offers other endemic countries.

account.outcome: On 16 November 2026 the World Health Organization announced that it had validated Eritrea as having eliminated trachoma as a public health problem. Eritrea became the 11th country in WHO's African Region and the 34th worldwide to reach this milestone. Baseline surveys were carried out between 2006 and 2020, all 58 sub-zobas were surveyed, and WHO's SAFE strategy of surgery, antibiotics, facial cleanliness and environmental improvement was applied wherever the disease was endemic.
account.significance: Trachoma is the world's leading infectious cause of blindness. Eritrea relied on community-led sanitation with limited external funding, together with donated azithromycin.
account.longTerm: The result adds to a steady fall in the global trachoma burden and shows that elimination is achievable in remote, resource-limited settings. Sustaining it depends on continued surveillance and care for new cases of trichiasis.

title: United States, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles elimination status

scores.rationale: The determination concerns three countries with a combined population of more than 470 million and reflects ongoing outbreaks with deaths. Long-term significance lies in what it indicates about declining vaccination coverage and the effort required to restore elimination.

account.outcome: On 17 November 2026 the Pan American Health Organization announced that endemic measles transmission had been re-established in Bolivia, Mexico and the United States, which therefore lost their measles elimination status. The decision followed the 10–13 November meeting of PAHO's regional re-verification commission. The United States had held the status since 2000. As of 13 November, the Americas had reported 58,213 confirmed measles cases and 82 deaths in 2026.
account.significance: Elimination means that measles no longer circulates continuously within a country; it is lost when a chain of transmission persists for more than twelve months. Kindergarten MMR vaccination coverage in the United States fell from 95% in 2019–2020 to about 92% in 2025–2026.
account.longTerm: The loss reverses one of the region's principal public health achievements. Regaining the status requires a corrective plan and sustained coverage of at least 95% with two vaccine doses in every community.
